board_events.text: Count the carbon groups ON nitrogen — never the carbon that carries it.
tert-Butylamine is 1°: only one carbon group touches N.
The nitrogen is an accountant — it counts only what is bonded to itself.
A quaternary ammonium ion needs four C-groups and carries a permanent $+$ charge.

segments.text: Let's start at the foundation. An amine is nothing more than substituted ammonia.
Take ammonia, N H three, and swap one, two or three of its hydrogen arms for carbon-bearing groups.
One carbon group gives a primary amine, two gives secondary, three gives tertiary, and four gives a charged quaternary ion.
Keep these general formulas ready: R N H two is primary, R two N H secondary, R three N tertiary, and R four N plus quaternary.
Here is the one rule that runs the whole chapter: we count the carbon groups on nitrogen, never the carbon that carries it.
<excited>That is why tert-butylamine is primary</excited> — only one carbon group actually touches the nitrogen.
Think of nitrogen as an accountant — it counts only what is bonded directly to itself, nothing further down the chain.
And a quaternary ammonium ion needs four carbon groups, which is why it carries a permanent positive charge.
<curious>To samajhte hain amines kya hote hain.</curious> Amine basically ek substituted ammonia hai.
Ammonia lo, N H three, aur uske ek, do ya teen hydrogen arms ko carbon groups se replace kar do.
Dekhiye — ek carbon group lagne par primary, do par secondary, teen par tertiary, aur chaar par quaternary ion banta hai.
General formulas yaad rakho: R N H two primary, R two N H secondary, R three N tertiary, aur R four N plus quaternary.
Sabse important rule: hum nitrogen ke upar lage carbon groups ginte hain, us carbon ko nahi jispe nitrogen baitha hai.
<excited>Isi liye tert-butylamine primary hai</excited> — nitrogen ko sirf ek carbon group chhoo raha hai.
Soch ke dekho, nitrogen ek accountant hai — wo sirf apne se directly juda hua cheez count karta hai.
Aur quaternary ammonium ion ke liye chaar carbon groups chahiye, aur ispe ek permanent positive charge hota hai.

board_events.text: Chain isomers: same class, different skeleton — butan-1-amine versus two-methylpropan-1-amine.
Position isomers: same skeleton, nitrogen on a different carbon — butan-1-amine versus butan-2-amine.
Metamers are the signature amine trick: redistribute alkyl groups across N to change the class.
$C_4H_{11}N$ gives eight isomeric amines; $C_3H_9N$ gives four — two 1°, one 2°, one 3°.
You cannot build a quaternary salt from $C_3H_9N$ — that needs four carbon groups, so at least four carbons.

segments.text: Amines also sort into two families by neighbourhood.
If every carbon on nitrogen belongs to a chain, it is aliphatic, like ethanamine; if nitrogen sits on a benzene ring, it is an arylamine, like aniline.
Look at this — a single formula, C three H nine N, hides four different amines spread across the classes.
Chain isomers keep the class but change the skeleton, as in butan-one-amine versus two-methylpropan-one-amine.
Position isomers keep the skeleton but move nitrogen to a different carbon, as in butan-one-amine versus butan-two-amine.
Metamers are the signature amine trick — redistribute the alkyl groups across nitrogen and you change the class itself.
C four H eleven N gives eight isomeric amines; the smaller C three H nine N gives four — two primary, one secondary, one tertiary.
But you cannot build a quaternary salt from C three H nine N — that needs four carbon groups, so at least four carbons.
Amines do families mein aate hain — neighbourhood ke hisaab se.
Agar nitrogen pe lage saare carbon chain ka hissa hain to aliphatic, jaise ethanamine; agar nitrogen benzene ring pe seedha baitha hai to arylamine, jaise aniline.
Yeh dekho — C three H nine N se poore chaar isomeric amines bante hain, sabhi classes mein bant kar.
Chain isomers matlab same class par carbon skeleton alag — butan-one-amine banaam two-methylpropan-one-amine.
Position isomers matlab skeleton same par nitrogen dusre carbon pe — butan-one-amine banaam butan-two-amine.
Metamers amines ka signature trick hai — alkyl groups ko nitrogen par baant kar class hi badal do.
C four H eleven N se aath amines nikalte hain, aur C three H nine N se chaar — do primary, ek secondary, ek tertiary.
Par C three H nine N se quaternary salt nahi banega — uske liye chaar carbon groups chahiye, yaani kam se kam chaar carbon.

board_events.text: Three sigma bonds form the base of a tripod; the lone pair points up out of the apex.
A tertiary amine $R_1R_2R_3N$ looks chiral, yet it cannot be resolved.
The molecule turns itself inside-out like an umbrella in a storm — this is nitrogen inversion.
Inversion interconverts the two mirror images millions of times a second at room temperature.
So treat amine nitrogen as configurationally unstable unless it is quaternised or locked in a rigid ring.

segments.text: Now the shape of that nitrogen.
Amine nitrogen is s p three hybridised and pyramidal, exactly like ammonia, with a bond angle close to one hundred eight degrees.
Three sigma bonds form the base of a tripod, and the lone pair points up out of the apex.
<curious>Here is a puzzle</curious> — a tertiary amine with three different groups looks chiral, yet it cannot be resolved.
The molecule turns itself inside-out, like an umbrella flipping in a storm; we call this nitrogen inversion.
Inversion interconverts the two mirror images millions of times a second at room temperature.
So treat amine nitrogen as configurationally unstable, unless it is quaternised or locked inside a rigid ring.
One more thing to file away: in arylamines the lone pair sits one bond from the ring and drifts into conjugation with it.
Ab nitrogen ka shape samajhte hain.
Amine ka nitrogen S P three hybridised aur pyramidal hota hai, bilkul ammonia jaisa, bond angle around one hundred eight degrees.
Teen sigma bonds ek tripod ka base banate hain, aur lone pair apex se upar ki taraf nikalta hai.
Ek tertiary amine R one R two R three N dekhne mein chiral lagta hai, phir bhi resolve nahi hota.
<curious>Kyun?</curious> Kyunki molecule apne aap ko ulta-pulta kar leta hai, jaise toofan mein chhata palat jaaye — isko nitrogen inversion kehte hain.
Yeh inversion dono mirror images ko room temperature par ek second mein millions of times aage-peeche flip karta rehta hai.
Isliye amine nitrogen ko configurationally unstable maano, jab tak wo quaternised ya kisi rigid ring mein locked na ho.
Aur arylamine mein lone pair ring ke ek bond door hota hai, isliye wo conjugation mein chala jaata hai — aage kaam aayega.

board_events.text: I U P A C: drop the terminal -e of the parent alkane, add -amine, and give nitrogen the lowest locant.
So ethanamine, propan-1-amine, propan-2-amine — the locant tells you which carbon carries nitrogen.
For 2° and 3° amines the longest chain is the parent; extra groups on N take an italic $N$- prefix, as in $N$-methylethanamine.
Diamines keep the -e: hexane-1,6-diamine, not hexan-1,6-diamine.
Aniline is a retained I U P A C name; substituted rings build on it — four-bromoaniline, $N,N$-dimethylaniline.

segments.text: Naming amines uses two systems, and both are worth knowing.
In the common system, name the alkyl groups on nitrogen alphabetically, then add -amine as a single word, using di- or tri- for identical groups.
In this structure the parent chain is highlighted in blue, and the full name is two-methylpropan-one-amine.
In I U P A C naming, drop the terminal -e of the parent alkane, add -amine, and give nitrogen the lowest possible locant.
So we get ethanamine, propan-one-amine, propan-two-amine — the locant tells you which carbon carries the nitrogen.
For secondary and tertiary amines the longest chain is the parent, and extra groups on nitrogen take an italic N prefix, as in N-methylethanamine.
Diamines keep the -e — hexane-one-six-diamine, not hexan.
Aniline is a retained I U P A C name, and substituted rings build on it, giving four-bromoaniline or N N-dimethylaniline.
Amines ko naam dene ke do systems hain.
Common system mein nitrogen pe lage alkyl groups ko alphabetical order mein likho, phir ek hi word mein -amine jodo, aur same groups ke liye di ya tri lagao.
Yeh dekho — parent chain blue mein highlight hai, aur naam banta hai two-methylpropan-one-amine.
I U P A C mein parent alkane ka aakhri -e hatao, -amine jodo, aur nitrogen ko lowest locant do.
Isliye ethanamine, propan-one-amine, propan-two-amine — locant batata hai kaunsa carbon nitrogen carry kar raha hai.
Secondary aur tertiary ke liye longest chain parent banta hai, baaki N-groups italic N prefix lete hain, jaise N-methylethanamine.
Diamines mein -e rehne dete hain — hexane-one-six-diamine, hexan nahi.
Aniline ek retained I U P A C naam hai; substituted rings ispe bante hain — four-bromoaniline, N N-dimethylaniline.

board_events.caption: Imine formed, then reduced

board_events.text: The aldehyde or ketone condenses with the nitrogen partner to an imine, a Schiff base, which is reduced in place to the amine.
The carbonyl fragment's carbons are all preserved, so the carbon count stays the same.
Ammonia gives a 1° amine, a 1° amine gives a 2°, and a 2° amine gives a 3°.
So reductive amination is the most general carbonyl-to-amine method — you reach any class by choosing the nitrogen partner.
In the lab, sodium cyanoborohydride is the selective reductant of choice — the Borch variant.

segments.text: The most general route of all is reductive amination.
R-C H O plus ammonia gives an imine, R-C H double bond N H, which hydrogen over nickel then reduces to R-C H two-N H two.
See the two moves — first condense to the imine, then reduce it in place.
The aldehyde or ketone condenses with the nitrogen partner to an imine, a Schiff base, which is reduced right there to the amine.
Every carbon of the carbonyl fragment is preserved, so the carbon count stays the same.
<excited>Here is the power of it</excited> — ammonia gives a primary amine, a primary amine gives a secondary, and a secondary gives a tertiary.
So reductive amination reaches any class you like, simply by choosing the nitrogen partner.
In the laboratory, sodium cyanoborohydride is the selective reductant of choice — the Borch variant.
Ab sabse versatile route — reductive amination.
Equation: R-C H O plus ammonia se R-C H double bond N H, phir hydrogen over nickel se R-C H two-N H two.
Yeh dekho — pehle imine banta hai, phir reduce hota hai.

Isliye reductive amination sabse general carbonyl-to-amine method hai — nitrogen partner choose karke koi bhi class paa sakte ho.

segments.text: Let's put every preparation route on one board.
Ammonolysis: R-X with excess ammonia gives the primary amine, along with some secondary, tertiary and quaternary.

Gabriel, same carbon and primary only: R-X becomes R-N H two.
Hofmann, minus one carbon: R-C O N H two with bromine and four K O H gives R-N H two.
Reductive amination: a ketone or aldehyde with ammonia or an amine, over hydrogen and nickel, gives an amine.

segments.text: A C B S E favourite — prepare butan-one-amine from one-bromobutane by Gabriel synthesis.

Step one: phthalimide with alcoholic K O H gives potassium phthalimide.
Step two: potassium phthalimide plus one-bromobutane, an S N two displacement, gives N-butylphthalimide and potassium bromide.
Step three: N-butylphthalimide with warm acid hydrolyses to butan-one-amine.
The by-product the question asks for is phthalic acid.
The amine has four carbons, exactly matching the halide, which confirms that Gabriel preserves carbons.
We choose Gabriel here precisely because it delivers a pure primary amine, with no secondary or tertiary contamination.
C B S E board question — one-bromobutane se butan-one-amine banao.
Yeh dekho — is target ke liye teen steps.
Step one: phthalimide plus alcoholic KOH se potassium phthalimide.
Step two: potassium phthalimide plus one-bromobutane, ek S N two displacement, se N-butylphthalimide plus KBr.

Amine ka carbon count halide ke barabar hai, chaar carbon — Gabriel carbon preserve karta hai.

board_events.text: Gabriel's decisive step is an S N two on $R	ext{-}X$, so strike out anything that cannot do S N two.
Aniline needs an aryl halide — aryl halides do not do S N two, so it fails.
tert-Butylamine needs a 3° halide, which eliminates instead of substituting — it fails too.
Benzylamine uses a 1° benzylic halide, a superb S N two substrate — it works.
Propan-1-amine uses a plain 1° halide — it works.
Answer: benzylamine and propan-1-amine. “Aromatic 1° amines by Gabriel” is a perennial false statement.

segments.text: A N E E T speed trap — which of benzylamine, aniline, tert-butylamine and propan-one-amine can Gabriel actually make?
Tick only the substrates that can undergo S N two.
Gabriel's decisive step is an S N two on R-X, so strike out anything that cannot do S N two.
Aniline would need an aryl halide, and aryl halides do not do S N two, so it fails.
tert-Butylamine would need a tertiary halide, which eliminates instead of substituting, so it fails too.
Benzylamine uses a primary benzylic halide, a superb S N two substrate, so it works.
Propan-one-amine uses a plain primary halide, so it works as well.
The answer is benzylamine and propan-one-amine; the claim that aromatic primary amines come from Gabriel is a perennial false statement.
N E E T speed trap — in mein se kaunse Gabriel se ban sakte hain: benzylamine, aniline, tert-butylamine, propan-one-amine?

Gabriel ka decisive step R-X pe S N two hai, isliye jo bhi S N two nahi kar sakta usko strike out kar do.
Aniline ko aryl halide chahiye — aryl halides S N two nahi karte, isliye yeh fail.

Benzylamine primary benzylic halide use karta hai, ek behtareen S N two substrate — yeh chalta hai.
Propan-one-amine ek simple primary halide use karta hai — yeh bhi chalta hai.

sections.title: Pitfalls and the carbon ledger

board_events.text: Traps that cost easy marks
Classifying by the wrong atom: count the groups on nitrogen, not the carbon that holds it — tert-butylamine is 1°.
Carbon-count amnesia is the biggest trap: nitrile plus one, amide same, Gabriel same, Hofmann minus one.
Believing aromatic 1° amines can be made by Gabriel — aryl halides cannot do S N two, so the route dies at step two.
Reaching for lithium aluminium hydride on an aromatic nitro group — it gives azo compounds; use hydrogen over palladium or tin with H C l.
Pro-tip: before writing any multi-step synthesis, count the target's carbons first and work backwards.
Mnemonic — G, A, S, H, M: Gabriel keeps carbons, Ascent adds one, Same for amides, HofMann minus one.
Beyond syllabus for J E E Advanced only: Curtius, Schmidt, Ritter, Leuckart and Borch extend the toolkit.

board_events.text: This lifts their boiling points above non-polar alkanes of similar mass and makes small amines water-soluble.
But the link is weaker than the O–H bonds in alcohols, so amines boil lower than the corresponding alcohols.
Among isomers, boiling point falls $1^\circ \gt 2^\circ \gt 3^\circ$: a 3° amine has no N–H to hydrogen-bond with.
Lower amines are gases with a sharp fishy odour; larger ones are liquids, then solids.
Arylamines like aniline are colourless when fresh but darken on the shelf as air oxidises them.

segments.text: Almost every physical property of an amine traces back to the lone pair on nitrogen.
Because the N-H bond is polar, primary and secondary amines hydrogen-bond to each other and to water.
See the pattern in the bars — and picture the N-H to nitrogen hydrogen bond.
That lifts their boiling points above non-polar alkanes of similar mass, and it makes the small amines water-soluble.
But nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen, so the link is weaker than in alcohols, and amines boil lower than the matching alcohols.
Among isomers the order is primary greater than secondary greater than tertiary, because a tertiary amine has no N-H to hydrogen-bond with.
The lower amines are gases with a sharp, fishy odour; larger ones are liquids, and then solids.
And arylamines like aniline start colourless but darken on the shelf as air slowly oxidises them.
Amine ki lagbhag har physical property nitrogen ke lone pair se aati hai.
N-H bond polar hai, isliye primary aur secondary amines aapas mein aur paani ke saath hydrogen-bond banate hain.
Yeh bars dekho — aur N-H se nitrogen wala hydrogen bond imagine karo.
Isse boiling points same mass ke non-polar alkanes se upar chale jaate hain, aur chhote amines water-soluble ho jaate hain.
Par nitrogen oxygen se kam electronegative hai, isliye link alcohols se weak hai, aur amines corresponding alcohols se neeche boil karte hain.
Isomers mein order primary greater than secondary greater than tertiary hota hai, kyunki tertiary amine ke paas hydrogen-bond ke liye koi N-H nahi hota.
Chhote amines gases hain sharp fishy smell ke saath; bade wale liquids, phir solids.
Aur aniline jaise arylamines fresh mein colourless hote hain par air se oxidise hoke darken ho jaate hain.

board_events.text: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia, because alkyl groups push electron density onto nitrogen by the plus-I effect.
That plus-I also stabilises the cation formed after protonation, so the base is stronger.
Anything that delocalises the lone pair — conjugation, an adjacent carbonyl — sharply lowers basicity.
Anything that concentrates charge on nitrogen raises basicity; that is the master lever for the whole subtopic.
Aniline is the cautionary case: its lone pair drifts into the ring, so it greets a proton only half-heartedly.

It can hydrogen-bond, and it can be donated — to a proton, giving basicity, or to an electrophile, giving nucleophilic reactions.
Picture the lone pair as a shopkeeper's spare hand, free to shake yours.

That same plus-I stabilises the cation formed after protonation, which makes the base stronger still.

Anything that concentrates charge on nitrogen raises it — that is the master lever for every comparison here.
Aniline is the cautionary case: its ring borrows the lone pair, so it greets a proton only half-heartedly.
Nitrogen ka lone pair do kaam karta hai, aur dono samajh lo to poora subtopic khul jaata hai.
Wo hydrogen-bond kar sakta hai, aur donate ho sakta hai — proton ko yaani basicity, ya electrophile ko yaani nucleophilic reactions.

Wahi plus-I protonation ke baad bane cation ko stabilise karta hai, jisse base aur strong ho jaata hai.
Jo bhi lone pair ko delocalise kare — conjugation, ya paas ka carbonyl — basicity ko sharply gira deta hai.
Jo nitrogen pe charge concentrate kare wo basicity badhata hai — yahi master lever hai har comparison ke liye.

segments.text: Basicity has a famous twist, and it turns on where you measure it.
In the gas phase, rank purely by the plus-I effect.
That gives tertiary greater than secondary greater than primary greater than ammonia.
In water the order flips — watch why.
A second actor walks on: the protonated cation is stabilised by solvation, as water hydrogen-bonds to its N-H hydrogens.
A primary ammonium ion has three such hydrogens to be hugged; a tertiary one has only one.
Add steric hindrance from bulky groups blocking protonation and solvation, and the neat inductive order collapses.
So for the methyl series the usual aqueous outcome is dimethylamine greater than methanamine greater than trimethylamine greater than ammonia.
Basicity ka ek famous twist hai, aur wo depend karta hai ki aap kahan measure kar rahe ho.
Gas phase mein sirf plus-I effect se rank karo.
Isse milta hai tertiary greater than secondary greater than primary greater than ammonia.
Paani mein order palat jaata hai — dekho kyun.
Ek doosra actor aata hai: protonated cation solvation se stabilise hota hai, jab paani uske N-H hydrogens se hydrogen-bond karta hai.
Primary ammonium ion ke paas teen aise hydrogens hote hain hug hone ke liye; tertiary ke paas sirf ek.
Isme steric hindrance jodo — bulky groups protonation aur solvation dono block karte hain — aur neat inductive order gir jaata hai.
Isliye methyl series mein aqueous order banta hai dimethylamine greater than methanamine greater than trimethylamine greater than ammonia.

board_events.text: Arrange ammonia, methanamine, N-methylmethanamine and N,N-dimethylmethanamine in increasing basic strength in water.

Methyl groups raise basicity above ammonia through the plus-I effect.
By pure induction trimethylamine should top the list, but in water its cation has only one N–H to be solvated.

board_events.text: The order is guanidine, cyclohexanamine, four-methoxyaniline, aniline, then four-nitroaniline.

Cyclohexanamine is an ordinary aliphatic amine with a localised, plus-I-boosted lone pair, far more basic than any arylamine.

sections.title: Traps and the one-count rule

board_events.text: Traps and the one-count rule
Never quote the gas-phase order in water — solvation and sterics scramble it to about $2^\circ \gt 1^\circ \gt 3^\circ$.
Aniline's low basicity is resonance delocalisation into the ring, not an inductive effect.
Always protect aniline as acetanilide before bromination or nitration — direct routes over-substitute or give meta.
Tertiary amines give no acylation, no Hinsberg product, no carbylamine and no mustard oil — they have no N–H.
Before predicting any 'does it react' behaviour, count the N–H hydrogens.
Two N–H: carbylamine, mustard, alkali-soluble Hinsberg. One: acylation, insoluble Hinsberg. Zero: none.
Beyond syllabus for J E E Advanced: guanidine and amidine super-bases owe their strength to symmetric conjugate-acid resonance.

segments.text: This subtopic is the pay-off from the nitrous-acid reaction — the arenediazonium salt.
Think of that minus N two group as a molecular ejector seat.
It is bonded to the ring but desperate to leave as nitrogen gas, the most stable small molecule there is.
Because nitrogen is such a good leaving group, almost any nucleophile can take the vacated spot — fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, cyanide, hydroxyl, even plain hydrogen.
Only aromatic diazonium salts survive — the positive charge is delocalised by resonance into the benzene ring.
An aliphatic diazonium salt falls apart the instant it forms, which is why primary aliphatic amines with nitrous acid just gave alcohols.
Two reaction families fall out of the ejector-seat idea: lose the nitrogen in replacement reactions, or keep it in coupling reactions.
Even the aromatic salt is only metastable — kept cold at two seventy three to two seventy eight kelvin, used in situ, and never stored.
Yeh subtopic nitrous-acid reaction ka pay-off hai — arenediazonium salt.
Us minus N two group ko ek molecular ejector seat samjho jo ring se juda hai.
Diagram dekho — nitrogen kho do replacement mein, ya use rakho coupling mein.
Nitrogen itna accha leaving group hai ki lagbhag koi bhi nucleophile khaali jagah le sakta hai — fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, cyanide, hydroxyl, ya plain hydrogen.
Sirf aromatic diazonium salts survive karte hain — positive charge benzene ring mein resonance se delocalise ho jaata hai.
Aliphatic diazonium salt bante hi toot jaata hai, isi liye primary aliphatic amines nitrous acid ke saath sirf alcohols dete the.
Do families: A mein nitrogen kho do — replacement; B mein use rakho — coupling.
Aromatic salt bhi sirf metastable hai — two seventy three to two seventy eight kelvin par thanda rakho, in situ use karo, kabhi store mat karo.

board_events.text: The excess acid does two jobs at once.
It generates nitrous acid in place, and it protonates leftover amine to the non-nucleophilic anilinium form.
Without that, the fresh diazonium ion would couple with leftover amine — so the acid must be in excess.
Mechanism: the nitrosonium ion $NO^{+}$, then an N-nitrosamine, then a diazohydroxide that loses water to give $\mathrm{Ar\text{-}N_2^{+}}$.
The salt is used at once, cold, and never isolated.

segments.text: First, how we make the salt — diazotisation.
Dissolve aniline in cold excess mineral acid, then add cold sodium nitrite, holding two seventy three to two seventy eight kelvin throughout.
The equation: aniline with sodium nitrite and two H C l gives benzenediazonium chloride, sodium chloride and water.
The excess acid does two jobs at once.
It generates nitrous acid in place, and it protonates any leftover amine to the non-nucleophilic anilinium form.
That protonation matters — otherwise the fresh diazonium ion would couple with the leftover amine.
The mechanism runs through the nitrosonium ion, an N-nitrosamine, then a diazohydroxide that loses water.
The salt is used at once, cold, and never isolated.
Pehle salt banate hain — diazotisation.
Aniline ko cold excess mineral acid mein ghol lo, phir cold sodium nitrite daalo, poore time two seventy three to two seventy eight kelvin par.
Equation: aniline plus sodium nitrite plus two H C l se benzenediazonium chloride, sodium chloride aur paani.
Excess acid ek saath do kaam karta hai.
Wo nitrous acid in situ banata hai, aur bache hue amine ko non-nucleophilic anilinium form mein protonate karta hai.
Yeh protonation zaroori hai — warna fresh diazonium ion bache hue amine ke saath couple kar jaata, isliye acid excess mein.
Mechanism nitrosonium ion, ek N-nitrosamine, phir diazohydroxide se guzarta hai jo paani chhod deta hai.
Salt turant, thanda, use hota hai aur kabhi isolate nahi hota.

board_events.text: For chlorine or bromine, use the copper-one halide — this is the Sandmeyer reaction.
The same halogen can go on with copper powder and $HX$ instead — the Gattermann reaction, simpler but lower-yielding.
For the cyano group, copper-one cyanide gives the aryl cyanide — again a Sandmeyer reaction.
For iodine, simply warming with potassium iodide is enough — no copper needed.
For fluorine, precipitate the diazonium fluoroborate with fluoroboric acid, then heat it dry — the Balz-Schiemann reaction.
Reagent split: salt for Sandmeyer, powder for Gattermann — these give Ar–F, Ar–I and Ar–CN that direct routes cannot install.

Ab replacement family — nitrogen kho do, naya group daal do.

Iodine ke liye bas potassium iodide ke saath warm karna kaafi hai — koi copper nahi.
Fluorine ke liye fluoroboric acid se diazonium fluoroborate precipitate karo, phir dry heat karo — Balz-Schiemann reaction.

board_events.text: The diazonium ion is a weak electrophile, so it does electrophilic substitution only on strongly activated rings — phenols and arylamines.
It attacks at the para position, building an azo compound with the $\mathrm{-N{=}N-}$ bridge and extended conjugation — hence intensely coloured azo dyes.
With phenol in mild alkali, p H nine to ten, you get p-hydroxyazobenzene, which is orange.
With aniline in mild acid, p H four to five, you get p-aminoazobenzene.
Strong base kills the diazonium ion; strong acid protonates the amine partner — only the mild pH window keeps both reactive.
This coupling is the foundation of a vast class of synthetic azo dyes and several acid-base indicators.

Phenol, with its strong activating hydroxyl, sits far above the rest.

Nitrobenzene, with a strong deactivating nitro group, is last.
The answer is phenol.

board_events.text: In the Sandmeyer synthesis of chlorobenzene, sodium chloride alone gives only traces, but copper-one chloride gives a good yield.
Copper is essential because the replacement is not a simple ionic substitution — chloride is too poor a nucleophile toward the aryl position.
Copper-one acts as a one-electron redox catalyst: it reduces the diazonium ion, releasing nitrogen and generating an aryl radical plus copper-two.
The aryl radical abstracts chlorine from the copper-two chloride, forming chlorobenzene and regenerating copper-one.
Contrast: the Balz-Schiemann route is ionic — the dry fluoroborate decomposes thermally to an aryl cation that captures fluoride.
Same lose-nitrogen, gain-a-halogen outcome — radical path for Sandmeyer, ionic path for Balz-Schiemann.

sections.title: Diazonium pitfalls and pro-tips

board_events.text: Traps that cost marks
Never ignore the temperature window — diazotisation and use must stay at two seventy three to two seventy eight kelvin, or warming gives phenol.
Do not mix up the reagents: salt for Sandmeyer, copper powder for Gattermann, potassium iodide alone for iodide, fluoroboric acid for fluoride.
Do not try to couple onto a deactivated ring — the weak electrophile will not touch nitrobenzene.
Get the coupling pH right — phenol in mild alkali, aniline in mild acid; extremes deactivate one partner.
A dry diazonium salt can be explosive, so everything is done cold and in situ.
Trivia trap: diazonium salts give a negative Lassaigne's test — they eject nitrogen before the fusion can capture it.
For synthesis, work backwards from the target group to its spoke on the wheel.

Two N-H gives carbylamine, mustard and alkali-soluble Hinsberg; one gives acylation and insoluble Hinsberg; zero gives none.

Top traps: classify by groups on N; aniline weak by resonance; protect aniline before EAS; 3° amines fail the N-H tests; Gabriel fails for aryl/3°; $LiAlH_4$ not for $\mathrm{Ar\text{-}NO_2}$; diazonium gives a negative Lassaigne test.
Numbers: diazonium at two seventy three to two seventy eight kelvin; phenol on warming above two eighty three kelvin; coupling p H nine to ten (phenol) or four to five (aniline).
Stoichiometry: Hofmann needs four K O H; carbylamine needs three K O H; ammonolysis reactivity $\mathrm{R\text{-}I \gt R\text{-}Br \gt R\text{-}Cl}$.
